key_insight: APGEM adaptively selects error-mitigation techniques from QML training feedback rather than fixing one strategy for the entire experiment.
engineering_relevance: A shared feedback interface could let engineers reuse one noise-aware controller across supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, and hybrid quantum-classical learning.
method: Observe fidelity, entropy, reward or loss, and gradient behavior at each step.
Use a contextual bandit to select among ZNE, PEC, measurement mitigation, dynamical decoupling, and circuit optimization.
Adapt mitigation choices as circuit behavior and noise change.
evidence_signal: Across five paradigms and 80 algorithm-and-noise conditions, APGEM reached 95.5% of oracle performance and significantly beat six fixed strategies; on noise models from eight IBM devices, it reached 99.9% of oracle utility at roughly 13,000 shots for 3–8 qubits.
watch_item: Results on device-derived noise models and 3–8-qubit systems do not establish performance on larger circuits or live hardware with drifting noise.
paper_title: Adaptive Policy-Guided Error Mitigation (APGEM): A Unified Learning-Based Framework for Noise Resilience in Quantum Machine Learning
